normative_text: A Protocol Specification MUST possess one stable specification identity and MUST identify its specification version.

applicability: Every completed Privacy Engine Protocol Specification
normative_text: A completed Protocol Specification MUST identify exactly one published Privacy Engine protocol generation from which it derives.
A Protocol Specification MUST preserve the semantics and obligations of the published protocol generation from which it derives.

applicability: Every completed Privacy Engine Protocol Specification
normative_text: A completed Protocol Specification MUST contain the complete implementation-facing normative composition required to implement its identified published protocol generation without dependence on hidden repository context.
An incomplete cumulative Protocol Specification MUST NOT claim completeness, final publication status, or suitability as the complete conformance basis.

applicability: Every Privacy Engine Protocol Specification and every interpretation of it
normative_text: A Protocol Specification MUST NOT be treated as independent protocol authority or as authority to modify its source protocol generation.
A cumulative Protocol Specification MUST state its composition status, composed section families, deferred section families, and current completeness boundary.

applicability: Every semantic requirement composed into the Protocol Specification
normative_text: Each semantic requirement MUST possess exactly one authoritative normative home within the Protocol Specification, excluding every supporting reference from authoritative-home status.

applicability: Every statement in the Protocol Specification
normative_text: Every specification statement MUST be classifiable as normative or informative.
A requirement using `MUST` MUST be interpreted as mandatory throughout its declared applicability scope.
A requirement using `MUST NOT` MUST be interpreted as prohibiting the stated behavior throughout its declared applicability scope.
A requirement using `SHOULD` MUST be interpreted as recommended; deviation MUST be bounded, understood, and justified without violating any mandatory requirement.
A requirement using `SHOULD NOT` MUST be interpreted as discouraged; contrary behavior MUST be bounded, understood, and justified without violating any mandatory requirement.
A requirement using `MAY` MUST be interpreted as permitting, but not requiring, the stated behavior.
Implementation-defined behavior MUST be explicitly permitted, bounded by the applicable protocol requirements, and documented by the implementation.
Every normative requirement MUST declare a bounded applicability rule identifying the subjects and conditions to which it applies.

applicability: Every interpretation of a normative requirement
normative_text: A normative requirement MUST be interpreted using its identifier, requirement text, defined terminology, applicability rule, authoritative section, and applicable cross-references as one coherent requirement.

applicability: Every supporting cross-reference and informative statement
normative_text: A supporting cross-reference or informative statement MUST NOT independently create, modify, complete, weaken, strengthen, conceal, or relocate a normative obligation.
Every normative requirement MUST possess exactly one stable identifier in the form `PE-<SEMANTIC-FAMILY>-<NNN>`, and that identifier MUST denote exactly one semantic requirement.
A requirement identifier MUST NOT be changed because of editorial reordering and MUST NOT be silently reused for a different semantic requirement.
Every normative requirement MUST record its requirement family, strength, applicability, authoritative section, and supporting source traceability.
Every statement intended to impose an obligation MUST be expressed as a stable identified normative requirement rather than apparently mandatory prose.
The Privacy Engine Protocol MUST be defined independently of any particular implementation, application, deployment, transport, storage system, or execution environment.

applicability: Every published Privacy Engine protocol generation
normative_text: A published protocol generation MUST declare the complete bounded protocol scope represented by that generation.
Each protocol invariant MUST remain owned by the published protocol generation in which it is defined.

applicability: Every downstream specification, profile, implementation, application, assessment, and certification artifact
normative_text: A downstream artifact MUST NOT redefine, weaken, strengthen, omit, or silently reinterpret an applicable protocol invariant.

applicability: Every claim of complete protocol realization
normative_text: A claim of complete protocol realization MUST account for every applicable invariant and normative requirement of the identified published protocol generation.

applicability: Every application and implementation using the Privacy Engine Protocol
normative_text: Application-defined meaning and implementation-defined mechanism MUST NOT be represented as protocol-defined meaning unless the identified published protocol generation explicitly defines it.
A Protocol Generation MUST possess one unique and stable generation identity.
A Protocol Generation MUST contain one bounded and complete protocol semantic state.

applicability: Every incomplete protocol fragment or partial change
normative_text: An incomplete protocol fragment or partial change MUST NOT be represented as a complete Protocol Generation.
A Protocol Generation MUST retain the same identity through publication, coexistence, deprecation, migration, and retirement.
A Protocol Publication MUST identify exactly one complete Protocol Generation as its publication subject.
A Protocol Publication MUST identify the complete published material, generation identity, publication identity, and publication version required to distinguish its result.

applicability: Every incomplete or ambiguous publication occurrence
normative_text: An incomplete or ambiguously identified publication MUST NOT establish a Published Protocol.

A Protocol Publication MUST NOT be interpreted as Protocol Succession, Protocol Lineage membership, compatibility, deprecation, migration, or retirement unless those relationships are separately and explicitly established.
A Published Protocol MUST identify exactly one Protocol Generation and exactly one complete publication of that generation.
A Published Protocol MUST possess a stable identity distinct from the identity of its Protocol Generation and its Protocol Publication.
A Published Protocol MUST NOT be silently replaced, partially rewritten, or reinterpreted as a different generation.

applicability: Every published Privacy Engine protocol generation
normative_text: Each published Privacy Engine protocol generation MUST remain the protocol authority for its own identified semantics and obligations throughout its recorded lifecycle.
A Protocol Publication claiming completeness MUST contain or unambiguously bind every component required to reconstruct the complete published generation.
A Published Protocol MUST remain immutable after publication.

applicability: Every correction, clarification, or replacement affecting published material
normative_text: A correction, clarification, or replacement affecting published material MUST be separately identified and MUST preserve the identity and historical content of the earlier Published Protocol.
An incomplete publication MUST NOT be used as the authoritative representation of a complete Protocol Generation.
A Protocol Succession relationship MUST identify exactly one predecessor Protocol Generation and one distinct successor Protocol Generation.
A successor Protocol Generation MUST possess an identity distinct from every predecessor generation.
Protocol Succession MUST preserve the identity, published content, lifecycle record, and historical truth of the predecessor generation.
Protocol Succession MUST NOT mutate, rename, merge, delete, or retroactively reinterpret its predecessor generation.
Publication of a generation MUST NOT by itself establish succession from any other generation.
A Protocol Lineage MUST possess one stable lineage identity distinct from the identities of its member generations.
A Protocol Generation MUST be included in a lineage only through an explicit lineage-membership rule supported by the applicable succession structure.
A Protocol Lineage MUST preserve the separate identities and lifecycle records of all member generations.
A Protocol Lineage MUST NOT create, inherit, transfer, or replace the protocol authority of any member generation.

A Protocol Lineage model MUST permit independent Protocol Generations to remain in separate Protocol Lineages and MUST require an explicit succession relationship before placing generations in one lineage.
Lineage membership MUST NOT by itself be interpreted as compatibility, migration eligibility, deprecation, replacement, or semantic equivalence.
Every published Protocol Generation MUST possess a stable version designation sufficient to distinguish it from every other published generation.
A version designation MUST NOT by itself be interpreted as proof of compatibility, incompatibility, succession, migration eligibility, or semantic equivalence.
A change to protocol-defined semantics, obligations, validity, invariants, or permitted behavior MUST be represented by a distinct Protocol Generation.
Semantic change MUST NOT be introduced through silent mutation, editorial replacement, implementation variation, or reinterpretation of an existing Published Protocol.

applicability: Every classification of a protocol change
normative_text: A protocol change MUST be classified according to its semantic effect rather than only its label, release number, implementation impact, or publication format.
A claim of compatible evolution MUST identify the generations, requirements, subjects, and compatibility scope to which the claim applies.

applicability: Every implementation variation within one published generation
normative_text: An implementation variation MAY occur without a new Protocol Generation only when every applicable protocol semantic and normative requirement remains preserved.
A compatible successor generation MUST remain distinctly identified and MUST preserve every predecessor obligation included within the declared compatibility scope.
Breaking evolution MUST be represented by a distinct successor generation and MUST explicitly identify the affected compatibility boundary.
Compatibility MUST NOT be used to merge generation identities, mutate historical published truth, or conceal semantic change.
Deprecation MUST identify the deprecated generation, the effective lifecycle condition, and any published continuation or migration guidance.
Deprecation MUST NOT revoke, erase, mutate, or retroactively invalidate the identity, published content, or historical truth of the deprecated generation.
A published migration MUST identify its source target, destination target, applicability conditions, required steps, preserved properties, and explicit failure conditions.
A mandatory migration obligation MUST be expressed as an identified normative requirement with explicit applicability and requirement strength.
Migration MUST NOT mutate the identity of a Protocol Generation, Published Protocol, implementation target, conformance determination, or certification.
A deprecation or migration statement MUST NOT silently redefine compatibility, succession, lineage membership, or protocol semantics.

applicability: Every environment supporting multiple published Protocol Generations
normative_text: Coexisting Protocol Generations MUST remain separately identifiable and MUST retain separate applicability, compatibility, lifecycle, and authority records.
Coexistence MUST NOT be interpreted as semantic equivalence, automatic compatibility, shared identity, succession, or migration eligibility.
Retirement MUST identify the retired generation, retirement scope, effective condition, and consequences for future implementation, assessment, and support.
Retirement MUST NOT delete, mutate, conceal, or retroactively invalidate the retired generation or its historical protocol truth.
Deprecation, migration, coexistence, and retirement MUST be interpreted as distinct bounded lifecycle concepts.

The Protocol Specification MUST establish the downstream derivation rule requiring the implementation profile to identify the Protocol Specification and published Protocol Generation from which its applicable obligations derive.
An implementation MUST identify exactly which published Protocol Generation it targets.
A conformance determination MUST identify the implementation, implementation profile, Protocol Specification, and published Protocol Generation against which conformance is assessed.
A certification MUST identify the conformance basis and published Protocol Generation to which the certification applies.

applicability: Every downstream implementation or assessment artifact
normative_text: A downstream implementation, profile, conformance determination, or certification MUST NOT modify the identity, semantics, obligations, lifecycle, or authority of its referenced published Protocol Generation.

applicability: Every use of a canonical Protocol Specification term
normative_text: A canonical term MUST be interpreted according to its definition and bounded role in this specification.

applicability: Every downstream section, profile, implementation, application adapter, assessment, and supporting artifact
normative_text: Every downstream use of a canonical term MUST preserve the same subject, relationship, scope, and identity distinction established by this specification.

applicability: Every term that may denote either a protocol type or an occurrence
normative_text: A term that may denote either a type or an occurrence MUST explicitly preserve the applicable type-or-occurrence distinction.

applicability: Every specification definition involving a semantic subject, identifier, or representation
normative_text: The terminology used for a semantic subject, its identifier, and its representation MUST preserve those as distinct concepts.

applicability: Every alias, abbreviation, implementation name, application label, and editorial synonym
normative_text: An alias, abbreviation, implementation name, application label, or editorial synonym MUST NOT silently redefine, merge, widen, or narrow a canonical protocol term.

applicability: Every terminology decision and editorial reorganization
normative_text: Terminology or editorial structure MUST NOT introduce a new first-class protocol subject, lifecycle, authority, or semantic boundary.

applicability: Every permitted local alias for a canonical protocol term
normative_text: A permitted local alias MUST map explicitly and unambiguously to exactly one canonical term while preserving its protocol meaning.
Every established identified protocol subject MUST retain its own bounded identity according to its defined architectural role.

applicability: Every Protocol Action, Protocol Action Evaluation, Protocol Action Determination, and Protocol State Transition
normative_text: Protocol Action, Evaluation, Determination, and Protocol State Transition identities MUST remain mutually distinct.

applicability: Every Protocol Action Evaluation and its Protocol Action Determination
normative_text: Evaluation and Determination MUST retain distinct process and result identities while remaining two bounded aspects of one architectural model.

applicability: Every Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action
normative_text: A Protocol Operation capability and each Protocol Action occurrence classified by it MUST remain distinct.

applicability: Every Protocol Transition and governed Protocol State Transition
normative_text: A Protocol Transition mapping and each Protocol State Transition occurrence governed by it MUST remain distinct.

applicability: Every relationship between identified protocol subjects
normative_text: Every subject relationship MUST preserve its declared direction, bounded meaning, and participating subject identities.

applicability: Every protocol subject referenced through an implementation, application, runtime mechanism, or application interpretation
normative_text: A protocol subject MUST remain distinct from the implementation, application, runtime mechanism, and application-defined meaning through which it is represented or used.

applicability: Every downstream representation or reference to an established protocol subject
normative_text: Every downstream representation or reference MUST preserve the identity of the same established protocol subject rather than substitute a newly inferred subject.

applicability: Every relationship, composition, representation, and implementation convenience involving distinct subjects
normative_text: A relationship, composition, representation, or implementation convenience MUST NOT silently merge distinct protocol subjects or their identities.

applicability: Every proposed extension to the established protocol-subject inventory
normative_text: A proposed extension MUST NOT introduce a new first-class subject unless independent identity, meaning, semantic ownership, and irreducible lifecycle necessity are all established.
Every protocol identifier MUST possess one declared bounded role identifying exactly the subject or occurrence specified by that role.

applicability: Every identified protocol subject and its identifier
normative_text: A protocol subject and the identifier used to reference it MUST remain distinct.

applicability: Every protocol subject and its syntactic, serialized, stored, transmitted, or displayed representation
normative_text: A semantic protocol subject and each representation of it MUST remain distinct.

applicability: Every relationship between separately identified protocol subjects
normative_text: The identifier of one related protocol subject MUST NOT be substituted for the identifier of another subject.

applicability: Every identifier of a Protocol Action occurrence
normative_text: A Protocol Action identifier MUST NOT identify, encode, imply, or reconstruct the Private Actor who performed the action.

applicability: Every public Evaluation, Determination, and Protocol State Transition identifier
normative_text: An Evaluation, Determination, or Protocol State Transition identifier MUST NOT identify, encode, imply, or reconstruct a Private Actor.

applicability: Every implementation, transaction, retry, transport-attempt, storage, or diagnostic identifier
normative_text: An operational identifier MUST NOT silently become or redefine a protocol-subject or occurrence identifier.

applicability: Every protocol identifier outside its declared subject and context
normative_text: A protocol identifier MUST NOT be reused outside its declared role as a universal participant identifier, cross-subject join key, or cross-action identity mechanism.

applicability: Every permitted change of protocol-subject representation
normative_text: A representation change MUST preserve the identity, semantics, relationships, and bounded identifier role of the represented protocol subject.

applicability: Every Privacy Engine realization of a public protocol action
normative_text: Every realization MUST preserve the architectural principle `Private actors, public actions`.
A publicly visible Protocol Action MUST remain verifiable to its declared protocol extent without disclosure of the Private Actor.

applicability: Every relationship between a Private Actor and a public Protocol Action
normative_text: The performer relationship MUST preserve the Private Actor and Protocol Action as distinct subjects.
A public protocol-subject identifier MUST identify only its declared protocol subject and role.
A public protocol consequence MUST remain attributable to the applicable public protocol occurrence without becoming attributable to a disclosed Private Actor.

applicability: Every Protocol Action validity, authorization, uniqueness, and public-consequence rule
normative_text: A rule governing a public Protocol Action MUST NOT require disclosure of civil, wallet, enrollment, admission, application, implementation, deployment, or transport identity as Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every public Privacy Engine protocol surface
normative_text: A public protocol surface MUST NOT require or create a reusable public participant identity.

applicability: Every Privacy Engine protocol action governed by anonymous-participation semantics
normative_text: The protocol action MUST permit verification of its applicable validity properties without disclosure of the Private Actor.

applicability: Every public value and public protocol subject exposed by an anonymous action
normative_text: Private Actor identity MUST remain non-inferable from each exposed value or subject within the protocol-defined privacy boundary.

applicability: Every pair or collection of anonymous Protocol Actions in distinct action contexts
normative_text: Cross-action unlinkability MUST be preserved unless the published protocol generation expressly defines a narrower public relationship that remains non-identifying.

applicability: Every wallet identifier, wallet signature, wallet-derived value, and wallet relationship
normative_text: Wallet identity MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as anonymous membership identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every application identifier, account, profile, metadata value, and application-defined relationship
normative_text: Application identity or application metadata MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every implementation identifier and implementation-specific internal value
normative_text: Implementation identity or internal implementation context MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every deployment identifier, topology coordinate, service identity, and infrastructure relationship
normative_text: Deployment identity or infrastructure topology MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every transport identifier, connection attribute, delivery path, retry path, and request context
normative_text: Transport identity or delivery context MUST NOT be substituted for, used to infer, or represented as protocol identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every enrollment right, admission object, funding relationship, sponsor relationship, and associated provenance
normative_text: Enrollment, admission, funding, or sponsor provenance MUST NOT be carried into public-action identity or used as an action-layer correlation value.
An action-local public value MUST remain bounded to its declared action role, action context, and permitted protocol interpretation.
Failure handling MUST preserve Private Actor non-disclosure and the non-identity-bearing role of public values.

applicability: Every implementation, profile, application, conformance claim, diagnostic, and specification interpretation
normative_text: A Privacy Engine artifact MUST NOT claim anonymity, unlinkability, metadata protection, or transport protection beyond the bounded guarantees of the identified published protocol generation.

applicability: Every composition of publicly exposed Privacy Engine values, subjects, consequences, and records
normative_text: The composition MUST remain non-identifying for the Private Actor within the protocol-defined privacy boundary.

applicability: Every implementation-controlled identifier, timing label, diagnostic, serialization field, log field, storage key, route, and public response
normative_text: An implementation-controlled surface MUST NOT create an actor-reconstruction, provenance, or unauthorized cross-action correlation bridge.

applicability: Every privacy-sensitive field name, variable name, route name, log label, diagnostic, comment, example, test, serialization field, and specification term
normative_text: Privacy-sensitive naming and documentation MUST use neutral terminology that preserves non-attribution and the bounded role of each value.
Public observability MUST expose only the minimum role-bounded information required by the applicable protocol semantics.
A diagnostic MUST describe only the applicable protocol subject, status, or bounded failure classification without identifying or reconstructing the Private Actor.

applicability: Every request history, telemetry record, path-acquisition record, submission record, and operational history
normative_text: Operational history or telemetry MUST NOT create a persistent relationship linking private participation across protocol layers or action contexts.

applicability: Every public protocol response, log, status surface, and diagnostic
normative_text: A public surface MUST NOT expose unnecessary provenance, topology, route, provider, retry, fallback, or execution-path information capable of increasing actor correlation.

applicability: Every information crossing between Privacy Engine layers
normative_text: A layer boundary MUST pass only the minimum preserved output required by the receiving layer without carrying unrelated provenance or identity context from the preceding layer.

applicability: Every implementation composition exposing multiple individually non-identifying surfaces
normative_text: The combined surface MUST be assessed and preserved as non-identifying rather than relying only on the independent safety of each component.

applicability: Every informative example, supporting cross-reference, test artifact, assessment record, and documentation surface
normative_text: Supporting or informative material MUST NOT introduce a correlation or identity interpretation prohibited from normative runtime surfaces.

applicability: Every anonymous membership identity in the current published protocol generation
normative_text: Anonymous membership identity MUST derive solely from private `memberSecret` possession through `leaf = Poseidon1(memberSecret)`.

applicability: Every claim of anonymous membership continuity
normative_text: Anonymous membership continuity MUST mean possession of the same original `memberSecret`.

applicability: Every replacement of an active `memberSecret` with a different secret
normative_text: A different `memberSecret` MUST establish a different anonymous membership identity.

applicability: Every wallet, backend, application, deployment, transport, and heuristic recovery mechanism
normative_text: A mechanism other than possession of the same original `memberSecret` MUST NOT establish, reconstruct, or simulate anonymous membership continuity.
A membership leaf MUST remain bounded to membership inclusion, path acquisition, and private proof-witness use according to the applicable protocol semantics.
Enrollment or activation MUST attach membership only to the privately controlled membership material presented for that enrollment without importing funding provenance into membership identity.

applicability: Every enrollment right, admission object, funding wallet, sponsor relationship, and accounting state
normative_text: An enrollment or admission artifact MUST NOT be represented as anonymous membership identity or Private Actor identity.

applicability: Every public enrollment, membership-status, readiness, and application surface
normative_text: A public surface MUST NOT expose a reusable mapping from enrollment or admission provenance to anonymous membership or public action occurrence.

applicability: Every anonymous action type requiring one action per member per action context
normative_text: Uniqueness MUST be enforced within the declared `(actionId, member)` scope.

applicability: Every nullifier in the current published protocol generation
normative_text: A nullifier MUST be derived as `Poseidon3(memberSecret, actionId, SIGN_DOMAIN)`.

applicability: Every action-layer duplicate-prevention decision in the current published protocol generation
normative_text: Nullifier status MUST remain the sole action-layer duplicate-prevention primitive.

applicability: Every public nullifier and nullifier-status record
normative_text: A nullifier or its status MUST NOT be represented as Private Actor identity or reusable participant identity.

applicability: Every nullifier outside its declared action context
normative_text: A nullifier MUST NOT be reused as a cross-action join key, participant tag, continuity handle, or global identity mechanism.

applicability: Every wallet identifier, membership leaf, enrollment identifier, admission object, and application account
normative_text: A wallet, leaf, enrollment, admission, or application identifier MUST NOT replace the nullifier as the action-layer uniqueness key.

applicability: Every duplicate-status response, log, diagnostic, event, and read model
normative_text: Duplicate-status observability MUST NOT disclose or enable inference of the Private Actor beyond the bounded action-local uniqueness fact.
Scoped nullifier uniqueness MUST NOT be represented as one-person, one-human, one-wallet, or globally reusable participant uniqueness.
An Interface Contract MUST possess one stable identity, one bounded semantic role, and one version sufficient to distinguish its published meaning.
An Interface Contract MUST derive from exactly one identified published Privacy Engine protocol generation.
An Interface Contract MUST define its bounded input semantics, output semantics, Protocol Operations, externally relied-upon behavior, and applicable observable failure semantics.

applicability: Every Interface Contract and every concrete realization of it
normative_text: Interface meaning and concrete representation MUST remain distinct semantic and syntactic roles.
A Concrete Interface Specification MUST possess one stable specification identity, one specification version, and one bounded integration surface.
A Concrete Interface Specification MUST identify and realize exactly one governing Interface Contract.

A Concrete Interface Specification MUST completely define the operation names, invocation forms, field ordering, type constraints, encoding rules, result representations, and externally observable error representations required by its bounded surface.

applicability: Every Concrete Interface Specification and its governing Interface Contract
normative_text: The concrete representation MUST preserve semantic equivalence with the governing Interface Contract.

applicability: Every Interface Contract permitting multiple concrete realizations
normative_text: Multiple Concrete Interface Specifications MAY realize the same Interface Contract when each realization independently preserves the complete bounded interface meaning.
A representation-only change MUST preserve the identity, semantics, ordering requirements, compatibility boundary, and observable guarantees of the governing Interface Contract.

applicability: Every change to published Interface Contract meaning
normative_text: A change to published interface semantics, obligations, validity, or observable guarantees MUST be represented through the applicable distinct-generation and versioning rules.

applicability: Every Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
normative_text: Implementation algorithms, storage layouts, deployment topology, transport machinery, operational policy, and application-defined meaning MUST NOT become interface semantics unless the published protocol generation expressly defines them as such.

applicability: Every Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
normative_text: An Interface Contract or Concrete Interface Specification MUST NOT independently acquire, transfer, replace, or modify protocol authority.

applicability: Every public Interface Contract and Concrete Interface Specification
normative_text: Every public interface realization MUST preserve the applicable SF-03 and SF-04 identity, privacy, unlinkability, minimum-disclosure, and neutral-naming requirements.
A Protocol Surface MUST possess one stable identity and one bounded externally relied-upon capability scope within one published protocol generation.
A Protocol Surface MUST expose only the protocol capabilities, semantic guarantees, compatibility boundaries, and observable behavior defined for that surface.

applicability: Every implementation realizing a Protocol Surface
normative_text: Internal implementation machinery MUST remain replaceable when the complete published semantics and guarantees of the Protocol Surface remain preserved.

applicability: Every implementation detail behind a Protocol Surface
normative_text: Code structure, storage layout, deployment topology, relay selection, transport, persistence, monitoring, optimization, or helper naming MUST NOT become protocol-surface semantics merely because a current implementation uses it.
A Protocol Operation MUST possess one stable capability identity defined by one published Interface Contract within one identified protocol generation.
A Protocol Operation MUST define one bounded protocol-owned capability, including its applicable input meaning, output meaning, and externally relied-upon behavior.

applicability: Every Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action
normative_text: The exposed Protocol Operation and associated Protocol Action representation MUST preserve the RF-07 distinction between the Protocol Operation capability type and each Protocol Action occurrence classified by that capability.
The governing Interface Contract MUST declare the operation's applicability conditions and the semantic roles of every required input and Published Result.

applicability: Every implementation realizing a Protocol Operation
normative_text: An implementation MUST preserve the operation's published capability across execution and implementation variation.

applicability: Every execution or implementation variation realizing a Protocol Operation
normative_text: Execution or implementation variation MUST NOT redefine the Protocol Operation's published capability.
A Published Result MUST possess one bounded result identity and MUST identify the governing Interface Contract and Protocol Operation from which its meaning derives.
A Published Result MUST express only the interface-level success semantics, failure semantics, guarantees, and observable meaning defined by its governing Interface Contract.

applicability: Every Published Result and concrete representation of it
normative_text: Published Result meaning and its serialized, transported, stored, displayed, or application-facing representation MUST remain distinct.

applicability: Every concrete realization or translation of a Published Result
normative_text: Every concrete realization or permitted downstream translation MUST preserve the complete bounded meaning of the same Published Result.
A Published Result MUST NOT be represented as a Protocol Action Evaluation, Protocol Action Determination, acceptance object, rejection object, or separate Evaluation Outcome object.
A Published Result MUST NOT be represented as a committed Protocol State Transition or as an independently authoritative public protocol-state consequence.

applicability: Every application interpretation or representation of a Protocol Surface, Protocol Operation, or Published Result
normative_text: Application-defined meaning, terminology, formatting, workflow, or response structure MUST NOT redefine protocol capability, validity, or Published Result meaning.

applicability: Every public Protocol Surface, Protocol Operation representation, and Published Result
normative_text: The complete exposed composition MUST preserve the applicable SF-03 and SF-04 identity, privacy, unlinkability, minimum-disclosure, and forbidden-correlation requirements.

applicability: Every Determination and every later representation or realization of it
normative_text: Protocol-semantic Determination production MUST remain distinct from representation, serialization, persistence, publication, transport, operational delivery, display, indexing, events, logs, responses and application interpretation.
